note: Single source of truth for the state definitions.

states.label: Overview
states.summary: All electrodes the device can record, without any state assignment.

states.label: Focus / Attention
states.summary: Sustained, focused attention. Key indicator: frontal midline theta plus frontal beta.

mappings.note: Frontal midline theta rises with sustained attention and cognitive control.
Second generator of frontal midline theta, evaluate together with Fz.
Basis for the theta/beta ratio as an attention index.
Increased low-beta activity during active, focused processing.
Increased low-beta activity during active, focused processing.

states.label: Relaxation / Rest
states.summary: Relaxed wakefulness. Key indicator: rise of posterior alpha.

mappings.note: Posterior alpha rises in relaxed wakefulness, especially with eyes closed.
Posterior alpha rises in relaxed wakefulness, especially with eyes closed.
Occipitoparietal alpha as a sensitive rest indicator.
Parietal alpha rises as attention fades / during relaxation.
Parietal alpha (left) compare with P4 for lateralisation.
Parietal alpha (right) compare with P3 for lateralisation.

states.label: Mental workload / Working memory
states.summary: Cognitive load, Key indicator: frontal theta rises, parietal alpha is suppressed.

mappings.note: Frontal theta rises with memory and task load.
Together with Fz it strengthens the load effect in frontal midline theta.
Parietal alpha is suppressed as load increases.
Alpha suppression (left) as a load indicator.
Alpha suppression (right) as a load indicator.

states.label: Emotional valence (frontal asymmetry)
states.summary: Approach vs. withdrawal via frontal alpha asymmetry.

mappings.note: Left frontal alpha. Less alpha on the left = more activity = approach / positive affect.
Right frontal alpha, counterpart of the asymmetry index.
Additional left frontal site to stabilise the asymmetry measure.
Additional right frontal site to stabilise the asymmetry measure.

states.label: Vigilance / Drowsiness
states.summary: Declining alertness. Key indicator: diffuse rise of theta (and slow alpha).

mappings.note: Diffuse theta rise as an early sign of fatigue.
Centroparietal theta rise as vigilance drops.
Slowing of occipital alpha.
Slowing of occipital alpha.

states.label: Calm focus (SMR)
states.summary: Alert but motor-quiet state. Key indicator: sensorimotor rhythm over the motor cortex.

mappings.note: Sensorimotor rhythm (left).
Central SMR over the vertex.
Sensorimotor rhythm (right).

states.label: Motor right (movement / imagery)
states.summary: Movement or motor imagery of the right side of the body. Activates the left motor cortex contralaterally. mu/beta drop during movement (ERD), followed by a beta rebound (ERS).

mappings.note: Contralateral (left) over the hand area: mu ERD during movement/imagery. Beta (13–30 Hz) also drops, with a rebound after stopping. Primary electrode.
Reinforces the mu and beta ERD pattern over C3.
Posterior to the hand area.

states.label: Motor left (movement / imagery)
states.summary: Movement or motor imagery of the left side of the body. Activates the right motor cortex contralaterally: mu/beta drop during movement (ERD), followed by a beta rebound (ERS).

mappings.note: Contralateral (right) over the hand area: mu ERD during movement/imagery. Beta (13–30 Hz) also drops, with a rebound after stopping. Primary electrode.
Reinforces the mu and beta ERD pattern over C4.
Posterior to the hand area.
Extends the medial ERD pattern.
Extends the medial ERD pattern.

states.label: Creative thinking (divergent)
states.summary: Divergent, idea-generating thinking. Key indicator: rise of alpha over frontal and parietal areas.

mappings.note: Frontal alpha rises during internal, idea-generating attention.
Frontal alpha (left) rises during creative ideation.
Frontal alpha (right) rises during creative ideation.
Parietal alpha rises.
Parietal alpha (left) rises during divergent thinking.
Parietal alpha (right) rises during divergent thinking.

states.label: Excitement / Arousal
states.summary: Sudden sympathetic activation (joy, startle, fight-or-flight): abrupt rise in high-frequency activity with suppression of slow waves. Emotiv composite metric – the electrodes approximate its multi-channel computation.

mappings.note: Anterior frontal (left): rapid high-beta rise during arousal, alpha is suppressed. Emotiv measures widely in practice (including temporal T7/T8 not available here).
Anterior frontal (right).
Frontal (left): high-frequency activity rises phasically. Gamma (25–45 Hz) would theoretically be involved but is unreliable with this device.
Frontal (right): high-beta rise during sudden arousal.

states.label: Stress / Frustration
states.summary: Cognitive overload: sustained high beta without regulating alpha pauses. Key indicator is the persistent frontocentral high beta coupled with an alpha drop.
